timing: retrospective specification of previously generated candidate

sourceFacts.fact: Dystrophinopathies characteristically cause greater proximal than distal weakness.
Describing anatomical weakness distribution helps clinical localisation.

invariants: Both shoulder and hip regions highlighted on proximal map.
Both hands/forearms and feet/lower legs highlighted on distal map; no organs or muscles exposed.
layoutSpecification: Two full-body front-view simple modest child silhouettes in fitted plain T-shirt and leggings, symmetrical neutral stance and flat colours. Do not show skin muscles or organs. Left labelled 'Proximal pattern': semi-transparent teal highlights on BOTH shoulder/upper-arm areas and BOTH hips/upper-thigh areas, hands and feet unhighlighted. Right labelled 'Distal pattern': ochre highlights on BOTH forearm/hand and lower-leg/foot areas, shoulder and hips unhighlighted. Fine callouts left 'Shoulder and hip girdles'; right 'Hands and feet'. Title 'Where is the weakness?'. Bottom 'Distribution helps localise the problem'. No claim that any pattern proves a diagnosis, no disability caricature, no naked children.
forbiddenAnatomy: No claimed anatomical reconstruction, diagnostic image, histology or literal neuroanatomical pathway
No organ cutaways or invented internal spatial relationships

validation.sourceFacts: Checked against listed primary clinical sources during original topic review
validation.pixelChecks: Visually inspected: proximal highlights cover bilateral shoulders and hip/thigh girdles, distal highlights bilateral forearms/hands and lower legs/feet. Labels match regions; modest clothing and neutral poses avoid misleading diagnostic appearance.
